title: The bottom key bar shows the keys of the current state

proofs.run: read the shots r9-foot-list-1280-light, r9-foot-list-1280-dark, r9-foot-reader-1280-light, r9-foot-reader-1280-dark, r9-foot-composer-1280-light, r9-foot-composer-1280-dark (par-macshell J0.17, s.shot)
proofs.pass: the bar shows the keys of its state in both themes

owner: Two decisions are the owner's. (1) 'Shift-R Reply all' in the list and reader bars: the build shows Reply all only on Enter in an open thread, because Shift-R is the No Reply filter (J0.18); showing Shift-R would change the key map. Default taken: keep. (2) 'E Done' against the build's 'Mark done' (Superhuman's word): default taken: keep 'Mark done'. Then look at the six shots.
notes: Built and judged today: list set (E Mark done, R Reply, F Forward, H Snooze, L Label, Cmd-K Search + hold) and reader set with Reply all, composer set (Send, Draft, Discard, Pop out + hold), keys follow the preset: par-macshell J0.17 (checks/parity/par-macshell.py:331-370, cases foot-list-set, foot-reader-set, foot-hold-item-last, foot-composer-set, foot-keys-follow-preset). par-macshell is journey style: it prints only 'FAIL <case>' lines and the total, so the proof is the total with 0 failed and no FAIL line for those cases; the 3 not judged are by design on a hidden rig (Dock tile, full screen: par-macshell-main83.log), so the pass regex expects '3 not judged'. 'Every cap from the catalogue': i18n --catalogue (checks/i18n-check.py) prints 'catalogue: GREEN'; 'Mark done', 'Reply all', 'Hold for all shortcuts' each hold 14 languages in Sources/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings (checked). keycaps-check.py is the cap-name check (r83: 8 checks, 0 failed). Built on lane/gap-keys (checks/parity/par-macshell.py J0.17): foot-shows-all-seven-at-1280, foot-shows-fewer-hints-at-960, foot-hold-item-is-still-the-last-row-at-960, foot-shown-hints-are-a-prefix-at-960, and light and dark shots of the list, reader and composer states at 1280x820. Unrun: if all seven hints fit at 960 the 'fewer' case is red and the finding is the app's width rule (MacFootHints.fitting). main93 (hid-keys): the case foot-shows-fewer-hints-at-960 became foot-keeps-the-hints-that-fit-at-960: at 960 the strip is 726 pt (sidebar 200, list 320, reader 438) and all seven hints fit, so the app was right and the old claim wrong; the broken copy that removed the width rule is dropped because nothing at the smallest window can tell it from the app.
